## How to use this notebook

This is where you work out the questions for the **5. Wellbeing** page (`R/page_wellbeing.R`) before they go on the website.

1. **Pick a question** for each figure. Ideas: `docs/question_bank.md`. Variables: `docs/variables.md`.
2. **Work it out** in the figure's chunk below: numbers first, then a quick chart.
3. **Write the finding** under **Title** (one sentence that states the result) and **Caption** (2-3 sentences: what the chart shows, the key number, what it means). Say "is linked to", never "causes".
4. **Copy it into the page file**: the `title`, the `caption`, and your ggplot code as `plot = function(d) { ... }` (see `R/page_story.R`).

**Shared functions** (from `analysis/_setup.R`):

| Function | Gives |
|---|---|
| `summarise_question(data, "x", "y")` | Spearman r, r at similar income levels (beyond GDP), r within each income group |
| `spearman(data, "x", "y")` | n, r, p-value |
| `beyond(data, "x", "y")` | r after removing the effect of GDP per capita |
| `by_income(data, "x", "y")` | r within each income group |
| `quick_scatter(data, "x", "y", log_x = FALSE, log_y = FALSE)` | a quick exploratory scatter, to look at the data (draw the website's chart yourself with ggplot) |

Add, remove or rename the Q sections freely.

## Q1: Do countries with more equal healthcare report higher happiness?

Jacob's question (from `HealthEqualityVSHapiness.Rmd`). The chart code is the same as `health_happiness_chart()` in `R/page_wellbeing.R`; **if you change the chart, change it in both places.**

**Variables:** `health_equality` (V-Dem: is basic healthcare guaranteed to all? higher = more equal) and `happiness` (World Happiness Report life evaluation, 0-10), 2010s averages.

```{r q1-chart}
health_group_colours <- c("Lower" = "#86b6ef", "Middle" = "#3987e5",
                          "Higher" = "#0d366b")

health_happiness_chart <- function(d, by_income = FALSE) {
  d <- d %>%
    filter(!is.na(health_equality), !is.na(happiness), !is.na(income)) %>%
    mutate(
      # ntile(x, 3): 1 = lowest third of countries, 3 = highest third
      health_group = factor(ntile(health_equality, 3), levels = 1:3,
                            labels = names(health_group_colours)),
      continent = countrycode::countrycode(iso3c, "iso3c", "continent", warn = FALSE),
      tip = paste0("<b>", country, "</b>",
                   "<br>", continent, ", ", income,
                   "<br>Health equality: ", round(health_equality, 2),
                   "<br>Happiness: ", round(happiness, 2))
    )

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = health_group, y = happiness, fill = health_group)) +
    # outlier.shape = NA: no separate outlier dots, every country is a dot below
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.65, outlier.shape = NA) +
    # Jitter spreads the dots sideways so they don't overlap; seed keeps the
    # same positions every time the chart is drawn
    suppressWarnings(geom_point(aes(text = tip),
                                position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 1),
                                alpha = 0.65, size = 2)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = health_group_colours) +
    labs(x = "Health equality (thirds of countries: lower, middle, higher)",
         y = "Happiness (life evaluation, 0-10)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  if (by_income) p <- p + facet_wrap(~ income, ncol = 2)
  p
}
```

```{r q1, fig.height = 7}
summarise_question(d, "health_equality", "happiness")

# Happiness in each third of countries (Jacob's summary table)
d %>%
  filter(!is.na(health_equality), !is.na(happiness)) %>%
  mutate(health_group = ntile(health_equality, 3)) %>%
  group_by(health_group) %>%
  summarise(countries = n(), median_happiness = median(happiness),
            high_income = sum(income == "High income"))

health_happiness_chart(d)
health_happiness_chart(d, by_income = TRUE)
```

**Title:** Countries with more equal healthcare report higher happiness

**Caption:** Preliminary: the third of countries with the most equal healthcare report a median happiness of 6.3, against 4.4 for the least equal third (r = 0.68, 162 countries). TODO
